 Judgment
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed by the Petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner has stated that on 11.04.2023, at about 8:00 a.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-41-W-2037 on Kanakapura Main Road towards Kagglipura, near Thalagattapura nice road bridge, Bengaluru.

At that time, a tipper lorry bearing registration No.
TN-30-BA-4586 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending vehicle") came from the same direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries, and his motorcycle was also damaged.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Shankara Super Speciality Hospital,
Bengaluru, where he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
The petitioner has stated that at the time of the accident, he was engaged in the business of selling mosquito nets and was earning a monthly income of 30,000/-.
Due to the injuries sustained, he has suffered permanent disability, resulting in a loss of earning capacity and reduction in income.
He has also incurred substantial expenditure towards medical treatment, conveyance, and other incidental expenses.

On these grounds, the petitioner has sought compensation from Respondent No. 1 and Respondent No.
2 for the injuries, disability, loss of income, and other expenses incurred.
4. In response to the petition notice, both the respondents appeared before this Court through their respective counsel.
However, only Respondents No. 1, has filed its written statements.
Respondent No.2 has not filed any written statement.
5. Respondent No. 1 - Insurance Company filed its written statement denying all the material averments made in the petition.

It is contended that the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle; on the contrary, it occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, who suddenly stopped his motorcycle without giving any signal.

The Insurance Company has admitted that a valid insurance policy had been issued and was in force as on the date of the accident; however, its liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It is further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the policyholder failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It is also alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid and effective driving licence, and that the vehicle did not have a valid permit and fitness certificate at the time of the accident.

6. The respondent no 1 has denied the nature and extent of the petitioner's injuries, income, and treatment expenses, as well as its liability to pay compensation, contending that the claim amount is highly excessive, exorbitant, and without any legal basis.
Hence, Respondent No. 1 has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding the motorcycle TVS XL bearing no. KA-41-W- 2037 on 11-04-2023 about 8.30 a.m near Kanakapura main Road, near Nice Road bridge,
Thalaghattapura, Bengaluru District, only due to to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper lorry bearing reg no.TN-30-BA-4586?
2. What compensation petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?
8.

In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1, MRO is examined as PW-2,
doctor is examined as PW-3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.16.
On behalf of the respondents, no oral and documentary evidence is adduced.
9. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

10. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1:- The petitioner has stated that on 11.04.2023, at about 8:00 a.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-41-W-2037 on Kanakapura Main Road towards Kaggalipura near Talagattapura nice road bridge, Bengaluru.
At that time, the offending vehicle came from the same direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries, and his motorcycle was also damaged.

12. The petitioner has examined himself as PW1 and filed an affidavit under Order XVIII Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure in lieu of examination-in-chief, wherein he has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

He has produced police documents marked as Exs P1 to P7, such as the FIR,
complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, and charge sheet.
13. One Mr. H. Sharath, MRO at Shankara Super Speciality Hospital, was examined as PW2, who produced documents marked as Exs P12 to P14.
Further, Dr. S.A. Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon, was examined as PW3, and the medical records were produced and marked as Exs P15 and P16.

As per the wound certificate and medical records, the petitioner had sustained an abrasion over the left knee, abrasion over the left leg, and a crush injury over the left foot exposing underlying Mahadevappa vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185165249/
3 muscles, vessels, and bones.

sentences.text: The doctor has opined that injury No. 1 is simple in nature, whereas injury Nos. 2 and 3 are grievous in nature.

14. On the other hand the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle; on the contrary, it occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, who suddenly stopped his motorcycle without giving any signal.

15. During the course of cross-examination, a suggestion was made to PW1 that the accident occurred on a busy road and that, without giving any signal, the petitioner suddenly stopped his motorcycle, causing the accident.
It was also suggested that, although the accident occurred due to his own negligence, he had falsely lodged a complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner has denied all such suggestions.

Apart from these suggestions, no material admission favorable to Respondent No. 1 was elicited from PW1.
16.

Though Respondent No. 1 has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, as well as the nature and extent of the petitioner's injuries, he has not produced any documents or entered the witness box to substantiate his contentions.

There is no evidence on record to show that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, nor has any cogent material been produced to indicate that the accident occurred for any reason other than the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

17. Upon evaluation of the entire evidence including the oral testimony of the petitioner, the medical evidence of PW2 and PW3, the documentary evidence, and the police records it is evident that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The respondents have failed to produce any credible evidence to rebut the petitioner's case or to suggest any alternative cause of the accident.
18. It is well settled that proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are beneficial in nature, and the claimant is not required to prove negligence with the same strictness as in a criminal trial.
The charge sheet filed by the police further corroborates the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, this Tribunal holds that the accident in question occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said road traffic accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

19. ISSUE NO.2 :-As per the wound certificate and medical records, the petitioner sustained an abrasion over the left knee, an abrasion over the left leg, and a crush injury over the left foot exposing the underlying muscles, vessels, and bones.
The doctor has opined that injury No. 1 is simple in nature, while injury Nos. 2 and 3 are grievous in nature.

Due to the impact of the accident,
the petitioner suffered severe injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Shankara Super Speciality Hospital, where he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
20. The petitioner examined Dr. S. A. Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru, as PW3.

4 fracture of the fourth metatarsal bone of the left foot, in addition to the aforementioned injuries.

sentences.text: He stated that the petitioner was treated conservatively and underwent procedures such as suturing of the lacerated wound under local anesthesia and POP slab application.
21. PW3 further deposed that he had clinically and radiologically examined the petitioner for the purpose of disability assessment.
The petitioner complained of pain, difficulty in walking, climbing stairs, and an inability to squat or sit cross-legged.
Based on his examination, PW3 assessed the permanent physical disability of the left lower limb at 26% and the disability of the whole body at 13%.

22. During cross-examination, PW3 admitted that he had not personally treated the petitioner and had examined him only for disability assessment after perusing the wound certificate and discharge summary.
He also admitted that the petitioner was treated conservatively.
He denied the suggestion that the petitioner's difficulties were due to old age or that the POP slab extended only up to the knee.
He further denied the suggestion that the petitioner was not facing any of the difficulties stated in his chief examination.
PW3 admitted that the assessment was confined to physical disability and did not include functional disability, and denied that the percentage assessed for the whole body was on the higher side.

23. Considering that PW3 has not provided any specific opinion regarding functional disability that is, the actual impact of the injuries on the petitioner's ability to perform daily activities and earn his livelihood and having regard to the nature and location of the injuries, particularly the involvement of bones vital for mobility and balance, this Tribunal is of the view that the injuries sustained by the petitioner have certainly affected his locomotor ability and functional efficiency.
Accordingly, the Tribunal reasonably assesses the petitioner's permanent functional disability at 8% of the whole body.
24. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 57 years.

Ex.P.11 - Aadhar card of the petitioner shows that he was born on 1966, the same is considered, then age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 57 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 9.
25.
At time of the accident, the petitioner was 57 years old and he was selling mosquito net and was earning a monthly Rs.30,000/-.
It is asserted that he has lost his earning capacity and income due to accidental injuries.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023, notional income Rs.16,000/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.

26. Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
27. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:

Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that Mahadevappa vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185165249/
5 the functional disability of 8% is reasonable and just.

sentences.text: 28. The petitioner was 57 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 9.
The notional income taken as Rs.16,000 x 12 x 9 x 8/100= Rs.1,38,240/- towards loss of future income.
29. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the injury, which has resulted in difficulty in mobility and in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .35,000/-
would be just and fair compensation under the head of pain and sufferings.
30. Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .25,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
31. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on medical bills at Ex.P.9 for Rs.44,315/-.
On perusal of these medical bills, it reveals that the Petitioner has spent .44,315/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of .44,315/- towards Medical Expenses.
32. Conveyance, food and nourishment charges:
Ex.P.8 -Discharge summary shows that Petitioner underwent inpatient treatment at Shankar Super Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru from 11-04-2023 to 13-04-2023 i.e, for a period of 3 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .5,000/- under the head of conveyance, food and nourishment charges.
33. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in mobility and in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery, this tribunal considers the 2 months for rest is considered .

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 2 = Rs.32,000/-.
34.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
 Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount  No.
1. Loss of future earnings . 1,38,240/-
2. Pain and Sufferings . 35,000/-
3. Loss of amenities . 25,000/-
4. Medical expenses . 44,315/-
5.

Future medical expenses - 6. Conveyance, Food and . 5,000/-
 Nourishment charges 7. Loss of income during . 32,000/-

sentences.text: Liability:
It is already held that the driver of offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident.
Therefore, Respondent No.1 and 2 being insurer and insured are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observations I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
36. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.2,79,555/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 2 years and balance 75% shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
